title: MCI Officer Roles
description: Duties of the MCI sector officers: Incident Commander, Triage, Treatment, Staging and Transport. From the MCI Reviewer, Chapter 4 (MCI Officer Roles & Action Cards).

pearls.text: Establish and name command at a fixed, visible command post, and announce it over the radio.
Declare the MCI and send the METHANE report. Request more resources early.
Set the objectives: life safety, triage, treatment, transport and hazard control. Lay out the scene: zones, staging, the treatment area and the loading zone.
Assign the Triage, Treatment, Transport and Staging Officers, and a Safety Officer. Keep your span of control to 3 to 7 people.
Coordinate with fire and police under unified command. Stay at the command post and do not get hands-on with patients. Hand over command face to face when you are relieved.
Report to the Incident Commander, put on the Triage vest and take the action card. Get the area to triage and your triage teams, working in pairs.
Do a global sort: "If you can walk, go to the collection point", then "Wave if you need help".
Sweep the area systematically and triage every patient with START (JumpSTART for children) or SALT, per local protocol. Tag every patient and mark the areas already searched.
Do only seconds-long lifesaving interventions: a tourniquet or pressure, open the airway, position the patient. Do not stop to treat or transport.
Report counts by category (red, yellow, green, black) to the Incident Commander and keep them updated. Have litter teams move red patients to the treatment area first, then re-triage.
Report to the Incident Commander, put on the Treatment vest and take the action card.
Choose the treatment area: safe, upwind of hazards, next to the loading zone, with room to expand and one entrance and one exit.
Lay out red, yellow and green sections with tarps or flags, and a separate black area out of view. Assign a manager to each section.
Re-triage every patient on arrival and regularly after that. Give focused care that does not slow the flow: airway, oxygen, bleeding control, splinting, warmth.
Prioritize patients for the Transport Officer and request supplies through logistics. The treatment area is not a holding hospital: keep patients moving out.
Report to the Incident Commander, put on the Staging vest and take the action card.
Set up staging at a safe distance from the scene, with easy one-way access in and out.
Check in every arriving unit: unit ID, level of care and crew.
Crews stay with their vehicles, keys in, ready to move. Release units only when the Transport Officer asks for them.
Tell the Incident Commander when the number of available units drops to the set level, so more can be requested.
Report to the Incident Commander, put on the Transport vest and take the action card.
Set up the ambulance loading zone next to the treatment area exit, with one-way traffic.
Get each hospital's capacity and capabilities (trauma, burns, children) through medical communications.

Call units forward from Staging as patients are ready. Load red patients first and send each one to a hospital that suits their category, spreading patients across hospitals. Crews do not choose their own hospital.
Keep a transport log: tag number, category, unit, destination and time out. Update the Incident Commander on patients transported and still waiting.
